questions.subject: Acute Cholecystitis
questions.title: Indications for Cholecystectomy in Gallstone Disease
questions.originalQuestion: About gall stones, all are true except.

originalOptions.A: Any patient with gall stones should have cholecystectomy.
originalOptions.B: Acute cholecystitis may be due to other causes than gall stones.
originalOptions.C: patient with acute cholecystitis, should had cholecystectomy at the same hospital admission.

sourceAnswer.text: Any patient with gall stones should have cholecystectomy.

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Routine cholecystectomy is not indicated for every patient with asymptomatic gallstones. Acute cholecystitis is usually managed with early laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the same admission when appropriate.

optionExplanations.A: Correct as the exception: asymptomatic gallstones do not require cholecystectomy in every patient.
optionExplanations.B: True; acute cholecystitis can occur from non-stone causes, although gallstones are the commonest cause.
optionExplanations.C: Generally true; early cholecystectomy during the same admission is standard for suitable patients with acute calculous cholecystitis.

questions.subject: Cyanosis at Birth

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Peripheral acrocyanosis can be a normal transitional finding in a newborn. Initial management includes maintaining warmth and assessing the newborn; oxygen is not automatically required for isolated acrocyanosis.

questions.subject: Brucellosis
questions.title: Diagnosis of Brucellosis in a Child
questions.originalQuestion: 12 years old child, live in rural area complaining of progressive fever, headache, arthralgia, by exam he has splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, what is the most probable diagnosis:

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: A rural exposure with prolonged fever, arthralgia and hepatosplenomegaly is compatible with brucellosis, particularly in endemic settings and with animal or unpasteurized dairy exposure.

optionExplanations.A: Correct; the clinical pattern is compatible with brucellosis.
optionExplanations.B: Dengue can cause fever and organomegaly, but the described prolonged rural syndrome with arthralgia favors brucellosis.

questions.subject: Postpartum Pulmonary Embolism
questions.title: Recognition of Postpartum Pulmonary Embolism
questions.originalQuestion: 26 yrs old female, 1 week postpartum complaining of sudden onset of dyspnea, cyanosis, tachypnea, most suspected diagnosis:

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: The postpartum period is hypercoagulable. Sudden dyspnea and tachypnea one week after delivery are concerning for pulmonary embolism.

optionExplanations.A: Correct; acute postpartum dyspnea with tachypnea is a classic presentation requiring urgent evaluation for pulmonary embolism.

questions.subject: Peripheral Edema
questions.title: Next Investigation for Bilateral Lower-Limb Edema

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: With bilateral edema and no clinical evidence of heart failure or chronic liver disease, renal disease and proteinuria should be assessed; urinalysis is a basic next investigation.

optionExplanations.A: Abdominal ultrasound may be useful in selected cases but is not the most direct first test for renal/proteinuric causes.
optionExplanations.B: Correct; urinalysis helps assess proteinuria, hematuria and other renal clues.

questions.subject: Acute Epiglottitis
questions.title: Airway Management in Acute Epiglottitis
questions.originalQuestion: 5 year old child complaining of an acute high grade fever, drooling and painful swallowing, the child sits and leaning forward (tripod position) and has stridor, what is correct,

originalOptions.C: immediate laryngoscopy in the operative room

sourceAnswer.text: immediate laryngoscopy in the operative room

questions.correction: The source answer is acceptable in intent because controlled airway evaluation/intubation should be performed in a controlled setting by experienced personnel; however, direct airway manipulation should not be performed casually in the emergency department.
questions.correctedQuestion: A child with suspected acute epiglottitis should receive immediate controlled airway management, with intubation in a controlled setting by an experienced airway team when indicated.

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: The presentation is classic for acute epiglottitis with impending upper-airway obstruction. The priority is securing the airway in a controlled environment; unnecessary throat examination or agitation should be avoided. Lateral neck radiography and CBC should not delay airway management.

optionExplanations.A: Not first-line when the child has significant airway symptoms; imaging must not delay airway management.
optionExplanations.B: Not the priority and should not delay airway stabilization.
optionExplanations.C: Acceptable in intent if this means controlled airway assessment/intubation in the operating room by an experienced team.
optionExplanations.D: May be used as an adjunct in some protocols but does not replace definitive airway management.

questions.subject: Factor Xa and Thrombin Inhibition
questions.title: Anticoagulant Effects on Factor Xa and Thrombin
questions.originalQuestion: which of the following anticoagulant act factor Xa and on thrombin:

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Dalteparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin that potentiates antithrombin and inhibits factor Xa predominantly, with some anti-IIa (thrombin) activity. Apixaban selectively inhibits factor Xa, while dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin.

optionExplanations.A: Apixaban is a direct factor Xa inhibitor.
optionExplanations.B: Correct among the listed choices; dalteparin has predominantly anti-Xa with some anti-IIa activity.
optionExplanations.C: Dabigatran is a direct thrombin (factor IIa) inhibitor.

questions.subject: Avascular Necrosis

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Common associations include sickle cell disease, dysbaric illness (caisson disease), corticosteroid exposure, alcohol excess and trauma. Chronic liver disease itself is not a standard primary cause of avascular necrosis.

optionExplanations.A: Sickle cell disease is a recognized risk factor.
optionExplanations.B: Caisson disease/decompression illness is a recognized cause.

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Irregular palpitations in an older hypertensive patient are most consistent with atrial fibrillation among the listed choices.

questions.subject: Hyperglycemic Crisis
questions.title: Cause of Hypotension in Severe Hyperglycemia
questions.originalQuestion: 16 yrs old child with history of uncontrolled DM, presented to the ER, on investigation Random blood sugar = 650 mg/dL, Na = 123 the cause most probably cause of hypotension is:
questions.correction: The source wording is medically inaccurate. Severe hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis with free-water and electrolyte loss, leading to volume depletion and hypotension; measured sodium is often low because of translocational/dilutional hyponatremia.
questions.correctedQuestion: In a patient with severe hyperglycemia, hypotension is most likely due to osmotic diuresis causing marked intravascular volume depletion.

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Hyperglycemic crises cause osmotic diuresis, dehydration and reduced circulating volume. The measured sodium of 123 mmol/L does not indicate hypernatremia; hyperglycemia can produce dilutional/translocational hyponatremia.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect as written: hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis and volume depletion; it does not cause osmotic hypernatremia as stated.
optionExplanations.B: Unclear in source.
optionExplanations.C: Unclear in source.

questions.subject: Complications of Multiple Gestation
questions.title: Condition Not Increased in Multiple Pregnancy
questions.originalQuestion: Increased risk with multiple pregnancy all except:

questions.correctedQuestion: Which of the following is NOT increased in multiple pregnancy? (No single valid answer among the visible options.)

correctAnswer.text: No valid single answer

questions.explanation: Multiple gestation increases risks of hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, placenta previa and fetal malpresentation. The visible options do not provide a clear exception.

optionExplanations.B: Placenta previa is more common with multiple gestation.
optionExplanations.C: Malpresentation is more common because of multiple fetuses and limited uterine space.
optionExplanations.D: Diabetes, particularly gestational diabetes, is also more common, so this is not a clear exception.

questions.correctedQuestion: Which factor commonly contributes to medical errors in clinical decision-making?

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: Medical error is multifactorial. Fatigue, cognitive biases, communication failures, system design and workload can all contribute. The source does not provide enough context to establish one universal most-common cause.

optionExplanations.A: Age alone is not a standard universal cause of decision-making errors.
optionExplanations.B: Fatigue is a recognized contributor to clinical errors.
optionExplanations.C: Working alone can reduce access to support, but it is not a universally established most common cause.

questions.subject: Estimated Date of Delivery
questions.title: Expected Date of Delivery Calculation
questions.originalQuestion: About last Expected date of delivery, which is correct:

originalOptions.A: LMP give accurate results if irregular menstrual cycles

correctAnswer.text: Cannot be determined from the information provided

questions.explanation: The conventional estimated date of delivery is based on an average pregnancy length of 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the last menstrual period in a typical cycle. Ultrasound dating is preferred when LMP is uncertain or cycles are irregular.

optionExplanations.A: False; LMP is less reliable when cycles are irregular.
optionExplanations.B: False; first-trimester ultrasound can be more accurate than LMP when dating is uncertain.
optionExplanations.C: Correct; average pregnancy duration is approximately 280 days from LMP.

questions.subject: Relapsing Infection
questions.title: Organism Capable of Relapse After Clinical Recovery
questions.originalQuestion: which of the following organisms can relapse after disease recovery:
questions.correction: The visible options do not include the classic malaria organisms that relapse from dormant liver hypnozoites (Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale). Varicella-zoster virus can reactivate as shingles, but that is reactivation rather than malaria-type relapse.
questions.correctedQuestion: Which Plasmodium species can relapse after clinical recovery because of dormant liver hypnozoites?

correctAnswer.text: Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale

questions.explanation: P. vivax and P. ovale can relapse because of dormant hepatic hypnozoites. P. falciparum and P. malariae do not form hypnozoites. Varicella-zoster virus can reactivate as herpes zoster but is not the classic answer to malaria relapse.

optionExplanations.A: P. falciparum does not form hepatic hypnozoites and therefore does not cause true malaria relapse from liver dormancy.
optionExplanations.B: P. malariae does not form hypnozoites and is not the classic cause of relapse.
optionExplanations.C: Varicella-zoster can reactivate as shingles, but this is not the classic malaria relapse mechanism.
